title: Global Climate
standard_code: Grade 10, Quarter 1: Earth and Space Science
standard_text: Weather and climate; the greenhouse effect; heat transfer by air and oceans; the carbon cycle; causes and evidence of climate change. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 10, Quarter 1: Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Earth and Space Science): weather and climate, the greenhouse effect, heat transfer by air and oceans, the carbon cycle and carbon sinks and feedback loops. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Climate is the average weather over about 30 years.
key_sub: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared energy given off by Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather is what happens day to day; climate is the long-term pattern. Earth's climate depends on the balance between energy coming in from the Sun and infrared energy going out. Greenhouse gases absorb some outgoing infrared energy and send part of it back, keeping Earth warm.

The atmosphere and oceans move heat from the equator toward the poles by winds and ocean currents. Carbon moves between the air, oceans, rocks and living things; forests and oceans are carbon sinks. Feedback loops change the size of warming: melting ice lowers the albedo, so more sunlight is absorbed (a positive feedback).

Example

Ice reflects about 80% of sunlight; open water about 6%. What happens when sea ice melts?

More sunlight is absorbed.

Answer: warming speeds up (positive feedback)

Example

Is 'it rained today in Cebu' weather or climate?

One day, one place

Answer: weather

Common mistakes

  • Confusing weather and climate.
  • Saying the ozone hole causes global warming.
  • Thinking all feedback loops make warming worse: negative feedbacks reduce it.

faq.a: The fraction of sunlight a surface reflects. Ice and clouds have a high albedo; dark forests and oceans have a low albedo.

faq.q: Why does the ocean affect climate?
faq.a: Water stores huge amounts of heat and currents carry it around the planet, which keeps coastal climates milder.

items.q: Kenneth is collecting evidence that Earth's climate is warming. Which is the strongest scientific evidence?
c: One summer day was very hot.
It was cold in my town last Tuesday.
Mountain glaciers around the world are shrinking.
A movie showed a big storm.
items.e: Strong evidence comes from many measurements over many years, not one day or one opinion.

sets.title: Heat transfer by air and oceans

items.q: A steel bridge railing feels hot to touch at noon. Which process transfers the thermal energy mainly?
items.e: Conduction: through solids by particle collisions. Convection: in fluids by moving hot fluid. Radiation: by infrared waves, no medium needed.

items.q: Over about what time scale does El Niño and La Niña change Earth's climate?
items.e: Different causes act on very different time scales.

items.q: A pot of soup on the stove warms evenly from bottom to top. Which process transfers the thermal energy mainly?

items.q: Angel studies the Gulf Stream, a warm current. How does it affect climate?
c: It makes the coast of Newfoundland cold and foggy.
It makes Western Europe warmer than other places that far north.
It makes the coast of Peru and Chile cool and dry.
It brings warmer water and milder weather to southern Japan.
items.e: The Gulf Stream makes Western Europe warmer than other places that far north.
